summaries.gardner: Schwab is the top dog in a mature industry (US retail brokerage and advisor custody) with a strong client-first culture and founder Charles Schwab still co-chairman, but it is not an emerging-industry leader, its stock fell about 2.5% over the past year, and few commentators call it overvalued, so it fits Rule Breaker investing only partly.
summaries.buffett: Schwab fits several Buffett tenets: a simple, understandable business with a trusted low-cost brand, scale advantages, high returns on tangible equity (38% in 2025) and steady capital returns. Its dependence on interest earned on client cash and its 2023 deposit outflows show rate sensitivity, and at about 15.7 times trailing earnings the price is reasonable rather than a bargain.
summaries.munger: Munger would like Schwab's low-cost, client-first model that passes scale savings back to customers, a virtuous circle he praised at Costco. Inverting, the main ways to fail are a rate or funding shock in its bank and a loss of client trust, both manageable but real, as 2023 showed.
summaries.lynch: Schwab is a stalwart with a simple story: client assets grow every year ($13.33 trillion at September 30, 2026), and profits rise with them. Its trailing P/E of about 15.7 sits well below expected 2026 EPS growth of about 32%, a Lynch-friendly setup, though it is widely followed rather than overlooked.
summaries.fisher: Schwab scores well on Fisher's sales organisation, cost control and management depth, and it keeps adding products such as spot crypto (2026) and private-company shares via Forge Global. It has no R&D-driven product engine in the classic sense, and its margins swing with interest rates.
summaries.graham: Schwab passes Graham's size, ten-year profitability and earnings-growth tests (diluted EPS rose from $1.03 in 2015 to $4.65 in 2025) and has paid dividends every year since at least 2011. It fails the price tests: about 27 times average 2023-2025 EPS and a P/E times P/B well above 22.5.
summaries.thiel: Schwab is a scale monopoly-like leader in parts of its market with strong distribution, but it has no technology ten times better than rivals and competes in a crowded field with Fidelity, Vanguard, Robinhood and Interactive Brokers. Its durability rests on brand and scale rather than on a secret.
summaries.gerstner: Schwab shows the efficiency Gerstner prizes (a 52.7% pre-tax margin in Q3 2026, falling share count, $7.3B of 2025 buybacks) at a modest forward P/E near 12. It is not a beneficiary of the AI platform shift he focuses on, so it fits his value-discipline lens better than his growth themes.
summaries.druckenmiller: Earnings are accelerating (nine-month 2026 GAAP EPS up 36% to $4.53) with record client inflows, which Druckenmiller looks for, but results depend heavily on interest rates and Fed policy, and the stock has lagged over the past year. A rate-cutting cycle is a key macro variable for the thesis.
summaries.smith: Schwab is a good company by Terry Smith's measures: high returns on tangible equity, durable franchise and steady organic growth. But a bank balance sheet, cyclical rate-driven margins and volatile operating cash flow make it a less natural fit than the asset-light consumer and tech businesses Fundsmith prefers.
summaries.greenblatt: The Magic Formula excludes financial companies like Schwab because return on capital and earnings yield are not meaningful for a bank-brokerage. On simple measures its earnings yield (about 6.4% on trailing EPS) is decent, but it does not qualify for the screen.
summaries.akre: Schwab fits Akre's three-legged stool partly: a wonderful business with a strong moat, capable management continuing the founder's culture, and room to reinvest via buybacks and new products. Reinvestment runway inside the business is moderate, with most excess capital returned to shareholders.
summaries.pabrai: Schwab is a durable, well-run business, but it is not a distressed or overlooked situation: the stock trades near 15.7 times trailing earnings and analysts are largely bullish (18 of 24 buy or strong buy). The Dhandho asymmetry of low risk with high uncertainty is not present.
summaries.wood: Schwab is a traditional brokerage, not a leader in ARK's disruptive platforms; its 2026 spot bitcoin and ethereum launch touches blockchain, but it is an incumbent that disruptive fintechs such as Robinhood target. It fits ARK's framework poorly.
summaries.ackman: Schwab matches Ackman's preference for simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with high barriers to entry and a dominant market position. Its sensitivity to interest rates and the 2023 deposit episode are the main caveats to predictability, and at about 12 times forward earnings the price is not demanding.
summaries.sleep: Schwab is a classic scale-economies-shared business: it has used scale to cut prices ($0 online commissions, 75 bps crypto trading) while clients bring more assets every year. Nick Sleep would see a long runway but would note the reliance on interest income rather than pure customer savings.
summaries.valentine: Schwab is a mature public company, far from the large, fast-growing new markets Sequoia sought, though its original discount-broker model in 1975 was exactly the kind of disruptive idea Valentine liked. It fits his framework only historically.
summaries.nash: Schwab passes many of Nash's financial tests (high margins, revenue up about 18% in the first nine months of 2026, low short interest, high institutional ownership, cheap PEG) and scores about 85 on his categories. It misses on secular trend, a founder CEO, a bank balance sheet with liabilities nearly nine times equity, and a mixed earnings-beat record.

momentum.evidence: The share price closed at $91.96 on October 16, 2026, down about 2.5% over 52 weeks and lagging the broader market, falling 8% after Q1 2026 results.

g4.evidence: CEO Rick Wurster led record 2025 results and founder Charles Schwab and Walt Bettinger serve as co-chairmen, but there is no single famous outside backer or partner beyond broad institutional ownership of about 85%.

g6.evidence: Analysts are mostly bullish, with an average price target of $118.41 versus a $91.96 price, so the stock is not commonly called overvalued.

integrity.evidence: Management communicates openly through monthly metrics and business updates and returns capital steadily, but Schwab paid $187M to settle SEC charges in 2022 over undisclosed cash-allocation practices in Schwab Intelligent Portfolios.

safety.evidence: At about 15.7 times trailing EPS of $5.85 and 3.1 times book value, the price is not well below a conservative estimate of value.

fairprice.evidence: A forward P/E of about 12.2 against consensus 2026 EPS growth of about 32% and 2027 growth of about 22% is a reasonable price for a high-quality franchise.

mu5.evidence: Its brand, scale and sticky client base make collapse unlikely, but the 2023 deposit outflows and $10,575M accumulated other comprehensive loss at June 30, 2026 show a bank-funding failure mode.

ly3.evidence: The trailing P/E of about 15.7 is below expected 2026 EPS growth of about 32% and the 2025 GAAP EPS growth of 56%.

fi2.evidence: Schwab keeps launching new products, including spot bitcoin and ethereum trading in 2026, private-company access through Forge Global and expanded advice and lending.

fi3.evidence: Technology spending produced the thinkorswim integration and new platforms that support record inflows, but Schwab does not report R&D separately and is a fast follower rather than an inventor.
